subQuestions.questionText: A pointing device that allows for gestures like pinch-to-zoom and two-finger scrolling:
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: C Touchpad (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The digital divide can be reduced by …
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: C increasing access to ICT devices for all people (1 mark)

options.A: limiting the amount of information on the internet.
options.C: increasing access to ICT devices for all people.
options.D: increasing the use of online and offline resources.

subQuestions.questionText: A user who typically uses specialised software that requires high resolution graphics:
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: D Power user (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Which web browser feature is used for storing frequently visited websites?
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: A, B or C (all accepted) — A Bookmarks, B Favourites, C Caching (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: … reduces the size of data files by encoding information more efficiently.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: B Compression (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Citing of sources in academic work is used to …
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: C acknowledge the original author. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Company X installed a network to specifically save costs. What will be their primary motivation for using the network?
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: A or C (both accepted) — A To enable resource sharing, C To manage data security (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Software used to view the results of HTML pages:
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: D Web browser (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: … is a decorative letter that often takes up two or more lines of text, usually in a first paragraph or section of a document.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: D Drop Cap (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: … uses tiny droplets of ink onto paper to create images or text.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: D Inkjet printers (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Integration of two or more technologies into a single device. Choose the matching term from: A #Value!, B utility, C objectivity, D required field, E watermark, F GHz, G location sharing, H digital footprint, I configuration, J multipurpose, K GB, L #Name!, M WordArt, N plug-and-play, O drivers, P default value, Q accuracy, R convergence, S history, T geotagging.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: R convergence (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: A feature that creates a transparent image or text in the background of a document. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: E watermark (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: A property in a database that automatically displays a value in a field when a new record is entered. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: P default value (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The ability to present information and ideas in an unbiased manner. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: C objectivity (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The unit of measurement used for storage capacity. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: K GB (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Coordinates inserted based on the location of a device. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: T or G (both accepted) — T geotagging, G location sharing (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The setup of devices without the need for user intervention. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: N plug-and-play (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: A trail of data that a user leaves behind while using the internet. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: H digital footprint (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Displays when a function refers to a cell with data that cannot be used in that function. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: A #Value! (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Software that allows the operating system to communicate with hardware. Choose the matching term from the same COLUMN B list as 2.1.
subQuestions.memoText: Correct answer: O drivers (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the following statement is TRUE or FALSE. Correct it if FALSE by changing the underlined word(s): The CPU is responsible for processing instructions.
subQuestions.memoText: True (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the following statement is TRUE or FALSE. Correct it if FALSE by changing the underlined word(s): The Large-key keyboard is a device that would help blind users to enter data.
subQuestions.memoText: False, Braille (keyboard) (1 mark). Candidates must supply the correct term (Braille) to earn the mark — the word FALSE alone is not enough.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the following statement is TRUE or FALSE. Correct it if FALSE by changing the underlined word(s): Primary memory is used for storing all programs and data permanently.
subQuestions.memoText: False, Secondary (memory) (1 mark). Candidates must supply the correct term (Secondary) to earn the mark — the word FALSE alone is not enough.

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the following statement is TRUE or FALSE. Correct it if FALSE by changing the underlined word(s): Virtual reality (VR) refers to the technology where a person interacts with a simulation of a 3D environment in a seemingly real or physical way.
subQuestions.memoText: True (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Indicate whether the following statement is TRUE or FALSE. Correct it if FALSE by changing the underlined word(s): The research question is a question that is brief and to the point to cover aspects of a broad research topic.
subQuestions.memoText: False, Focus (question) (1 mark). Candidates must supply the correct term (Focus question) to earn the mark — the word FALSE alone is not enough.

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO disadvantages of using a wireless mouse.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Can easily be lost/stolen; batteries should be replaced often; prone to signal interference/disturbance; Bluetooth receiver can be lost/damaged then mouse won't work/device out of range of receiver. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain what biometric security is AND give ONE example of a biometric device.
subQuestions.memoText: Biometric security is using unique biological features to access devices/systems (1 mark). ONE example (any one): Fingerprint reader/scanner; Iris/Eye/Retinal scanner; Facial recognition camera; Voice recognition microphone (1 mark). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe the purpose of a UPS compared to a permanent power supply.
subQuestions.memoText: A power supply is designed to provide continuous power, while a UPS provides backup power during outages. OR accept any two aspects of a UPS: has a battery backup system; provides backup power during outages; protects your device against power surges; allows user to save their work before switching off the device. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Recommend THREE basic hardware components to consider when buying an end-user computer.
subQuestions.memoText: Any THREE: Processor (CPU); Memory (RAM); Storage (SSD/HDD); Motherboard; Graphics card (GPU); Network card (NIC); Power supply. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: A data projector has been set up and displays a 'No Signal' error. Identify TWO possible reasons why this error occurs.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Cable/signal (WiFi, Bluetooth, etc.) not connected properly; faulty cable/port; incorrect display settings (e.g. extended, duplicate, etc.); computer is off or on sleep mode; faulty/outdated drivers; correct source is not selected (PC/VGA/HDMI, etc.). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Describe TWO accessibility features that a deaf person can use.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Captions/subtitles for spoken dialog; speech-to-text; visual (flashing) notifications for sounds; motion (vibration) notifications for sounds. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: One of the functions of an operating system is to manage programs and users. Explain the difference between a single-user system and a multi-user system.
subQuestions.memoText: A single-user system is limited to only one active user/one user at a time. A multi-user system allows more than one user at the same time. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE example of where a multi-user system can be used.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Online gaming; online platforms; (networked) companies/institutions (e.g. school, university, banks, SARS, etc.). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO ways how a user can customise the graphical user interface (GUI) to suit their preferences.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO relevant answers, e.g. adjust screen resolution; change background; themes; font size/colour; brightness of screen; add/remove shortcuts/icons; format shortcuts/icons; custom keyboard; change cursor size/shape; system/notification sound; quick access menus; accessibility; multiple desktop; date/time format; notification tray icons. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Users are often at risk of using flawed (faulty) software. Recommend ONE way to fix a software bug.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Install a patch; install a service pack; update software. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO risks of using flawed software.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Security vulnerabilities (create security loopholes that attackers might use to gain unauthorised access); data loss or corruption; system crashing (the device can malfunction or crash, causing a disruption in normal operation); compatibility issues with hardware and software. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Motivate why using the hidden attribute will be better for protecting the data in a file compared to the read-only attribute.
subQuestions.memoText: Hidden: the user cannot see the file. Read-only: the user can see the file, but cannot change the file. OR any TWO: Hidden hides the file from view and layout, not visible to a user if show/hide is not enabled; Read-only prevents user from editing the file but can still be opened, immediately visible to user, can be viewed and copied but not edited or deleted without changing the attribute. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The utility feature shown below is used on a computer hard drive. The screenshot shows a dialog box titled 'Optimize and defragment drive', with a disk-drive icon and a single button labelled 'Optimize'. Explain why a user will use the feature above.
subQuestions.memoText: To reorganise fragmented/scattered data on a computer's hard disk to improve performance and efficiency/fixing disk errors. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Which communication medium is used for a high-speed internet connection?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Fibre optic cable; copper cable (coaxial); DSL (Digital Subscriber Line); Ethernet; radio waves 4G/5G/LTE cellular networks; satellite. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain what is meant by a wireless access point.
subQuestions.memoText: A device that allows other wireless devices to connect to a wired/wireless network. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: A network can be used to provide better security. Indicate ONE method that can be used to secure a network.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Firewalls; VPN; access controls/authentication/logins (username and password); antivirus or anti-malware security; use security protocols for password encryption; network data/files can be encrypted. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons why a company may choose NOT to use an intranet.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Company too small to justify cost of intranet/often tied to licencing (Office etc.); staff can bring in unauthorised devices and infect the intranet with malware; requires integration and maintenance; often overly complex for employees/inaccessible/challenging to access for employees working from home/personal PCs or smartphones/rarely equipped with offline functionality/employees need to be trained. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain what the Fourth Industrial Revolution (4IR) is.
subQuestions.memoText: Integration of technologies in the physical, digital, biological world. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO advantages of using tabbed web browsing.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Efficient use of screen space; faster navigation/saves time to access websites; access to more than one website; organise tabs in groups; allows multiple home pages that all open simultaneously; convenient for multitasking. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Discuss TWO factors that may decrease upload and download speeds in an internet connection.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: File size/multiple files open; bandwidth size; background applications running; the type of internet connection (e.g. DSL, cable, fibre); the quality/stability/reliability of the connection/network traffic/congestion; distance from the service provider/router; hardware capabilities (router, modem); shaping; throttling; capacity of the ISP's infrastructure; efficiency of the user's devices. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: John received an e-mail marked as high priority and decided to flag it. The screenshot shows an inbox preview from 'John Mokoena <john@...>' with the subject line 'Take note', received at 07:34, a red high-priority exclamation mark and a flag icon both shown next to the message, and the preview text 'Good day. Please be reminded...'. Motivate why the 'Subject' line is inappropriate.
subQuestions.memoText: The subject line does not indicate the topic of the e-mail. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Differentiate between high priority and flagging.
subQuestions.memoText: High priority: these emails are marked as important by the sender/should be addressed promptly. Flagging: flagging is a way for you to organise/categorise/prioritise/follow up or keep track of e-mails. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: State TWO ways to present research information to a target audience.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Write a report; create a presentation; create a website; podcast/vodcast; social media; printed media. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE reason why you would choose to use information from older sources.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Factual information that won't change; established authority and credibility of the author; historical information; the information is still relevant; can be compared to newer sources. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO guidelines to follow when setting questions for a questionnaire.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Use mostly closed questions; keep questions short; categorise/group questions; limit number of questions/time to complete questionnaire; use easily understandable language; relevant questions/target audience; give options to choose from; ask questions that will not guide people to specific answers/unbiased. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain ONE reason why a database instead of a spreadsheet would be used to process data collected during research.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Perform (complex) queries; to create reports with grouping/calculations; relate or link lots of data; amount of data is too complex to work with/view in a spreadsheet. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: You need to add an image to a document. Name ONE word processing feature that may be used to acknowledge a source for an image, excluding citations.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Bibliography; endnote/footnote; caption. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE example of the type of data you could add to acknowledge the source.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Include the image creator/author/photographer/artist name; name of image; website/hyperlink (URL) to the original source; date of creation, publisher. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Study the extract from the database report below. The report is titled 'Feedback' and lists participants grouped by Event, with columns Participant name, Participant Code and Age. Under the group heading 'Bike': Agnus (code Agnus1320, age 34), Clifford (Clifford135, age 25), Grant (Grant140, age 31), Hemlata (Hemlata434, age 30), John (John435, age 39) — a group count of 5 and an Average Age of 32 are shown beneath the Bike group. Under the group heading 'Run': Fatima (Fatima206, age 35), Kabelo (Kabelo144, age 28), Kholofelo (Kholofelo95, age 22), Louis (Louis254, age 23), Madeline (Madeline143, age 25), Meschack (Meschack160, age 48), Mohamed (Mohamed359, age 22). Give TWO findings of this report.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: The average age for participants of the bike race is 32; the number of participants for the bike race is 5; 3 of the participants for the bike race are older than 30 years/2 participants for the bike race are 30 years and younger; more participants in their 30's choose to bike; more runners than bikers. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: There are various types of viruses that affect a computer. What is a computer virus?
subQuestions.memoText: Software/program/app that is designed for malicious intent/unwanted/unexpected (behaviour). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain TWO ways in which a virus can affect the performance of a computer.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: File(s) become corrupt; unknown program(s) or file(s)/folders suddenly appears; additional programs start to run when the computer is started; size of a file changes without explanation; program(s) or file(s) are suddenly missing; program/file changes without explanation/stops operating properly; settings of security software changed/switched off; strange/unexpected message/pop-ups/image/error messages displayed on the computer screen; computer suddenly begins to start or run slowly; unauthorised changes made to the registry; available memory is less than it should be; system properties change; free hard drive space suddenly gets reduced; network performance is influenced; computer no longer boots. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Which term describes all the ways in which confidential information is obtained by abusing the trusting nature of people?
subQuestions.memoText: Social engineering. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Green computing should be considered by all computer users. Explain the term green computing.
subQuestions.memoText: Using computers in a way that is not harmful to the environment. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE energy-saving method that contributes to green computing.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Switch off devices/unplug devices when not in use; enable sleep/hibernate function if computer is not in use; reduce screen brightness; enable battery saving mode; use energy saving devices e.g. LCD screen, SSD. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Your friend wanted to download a song from the internet and clicked the download button, but was redirected to a malicious page. Give the term for the threat described above.
subQuestions.memoText: Click-jacking/Pharming. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Recommend TWO actions that your friend can take to prevent this from happening again.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Download songs only from well-known websites; verify that the website URL is correct and matches the official site; use browser settings that require you to click to play multimedia content; install pop-up blockers; use browser extensions that provide additional security features; keep your web browser up-to-date; before clicking on a download link, hover over it to see the actual URL; avoid clicking on any pop-ups, banners, or unexpected buttons that appear while you're trying to download; keep your antivirus software updated and running; check reviews and ratings of the download service or file before proceeding; ensure the website uses HTTPS. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Give a word processing feature that will allow a user to format all the headings in a document at the same time.
subQuestions.memoText: Styles. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Tab stops can be used to align text neatly in columns. Name TWO features that can be used to set tab stops in a word processing document.
subQuestions.memoText: Using the ruler; using the Tab settings dialog box. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: A leader line can be added with tab stops. Why would you add a leader line?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: To improve the readability/alignment of text in documents; visually connect and guide the reader's eye across the space between tab stops; to add signature/date lines. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Study the screenshot below of an agenda in a word processing document. It shows the heading 'Agenda' followed by a numbered/lettered multilevel list: 1. Welcome, 2. Attendance, 3. Minutes of previous meeting (with 'wrapped' text below it reading '15 July 2024' that appears indented under item 3 but is not itself a numbered list item), 4. Planning, with sub-items a. Term 1, b. Term 2 (with further sub-sub-items i. June exam, ii. Holiday classes), c. Term 3, d. Term 4. Which word processing feature has been used to create the list?
subQuestions.memoText: Multilevel list. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the date '15 July 2024' is not one of the list items AND how the date can be displayed as a list item.
subQuestions.memoText: The date is still part of the same paragraph because a line break/soft enter/Shift+Enter was used. A new number will only display for a new paragraph break/Enter. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain the difference between the <th> and the <td> tags.
subQuestions.memoText: <th> creates a header cell in a table/text that is bold and centred. <td> creates a cell to add data in a table. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Fields in a database table can consist of various data types. Explain when an OLE object data type will be used.
subQuestions.memoText: Used for linking/embedding/inserting images/files/videos as data. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO data types that can be used for text in a database table.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Short text; long text; lookup. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Which THREE functions were combined to extract the username from the e-mail address in the screenshot below? A two-column table shows 'E-mail address' next to 'Username': cateducator@school.co.za → cateducator; maths1234@school.co.za → maths1234; engpoems@school.co.za → engpoems; lifechange@school.co.za → lifechange. In each case the username is the portion of the e-mail address before the @ symbol.
subQuestions.memoText: LEFT (or MID); LEN; FIND. (3 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Your school is celebrating its 50th birthday. A committee has been chosen to create and design an e-magazine as part of the celebration. State TWO advantages for the committee to design an e-magazine instead of a hard-copy version.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Interactive elements; saving of printing cost; easy to change/update; reach larger audience/easier to share; saves the environment; accessibility features. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The committee needs to work on the same network system. The school has provided the committee with a wireless connection. What network policy should the school and committee have in place?
subQuestions.memoText: AUP (Acceptable Use Policy). (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain what a network adapter is.
subQuestions.memoText: A component in a computer that enables network connection. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why the network might be slow while the committee is working on the e-magazine.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Not enough bandwidth/network traffic/congestion; files being shared are too large; weak signal; faulty/outdated hardware; DDoS attacks. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The committee will conduct interviews with previous learners, teachers and staff for the e-magazine. The interviews will be conducted using video conferencing. State TWO disadvantages of using video conferencing.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Requires a fast internet connection; consumes a lot of data when using video/depletes CAP quickly; lack of physical face to face contact/non-verbal cues. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Name ONE good practice the committee should consider when conducting the interviews online.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Eliminate background noises; equipment must be set up correctly; make sure that the interview is recorded; make sure there is good lighting; speak clearly/audible. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Explain why interviews would be a better option to collect the information rather than using questionnaires.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Deeper insight/clarification and follow up; non-verbal cues; response is immediate; building relationships. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The committee will use a scanner to scan images and text for the e-magazine. What does MP stand for in camera resolution?
subQuestions.memoText: Megapixel. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Why would the committee make use of OCR software?
subQuestions.memoText: To produce an editable soft copy from a scanned document. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The school wants to scan photos of the opening day taken 50 years ago. Why would you not recommend scanning old photos?
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Poor quality scanned image; all imperfections (like tears and cracks) will also be included in the image; time consuming process; fragile photos might be damaged. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Photos that will be displayed in the e-magazine must be uploaded to cloud storage. State TWO advantages of storing photos on the cloud compared to local storage.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Convenient access from any device anywhere/anytime with internet connection; serves as storage space to backup; service provider may provide more security than local storage; saves local storage space on local device; synchronisation services between devices. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The committee will be using various software applications to design and organise the e-magazine. Name TWO types of application software the committee can use to design the e-magazine.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Desktop publisher software; designing software; presentation software; word processing software; web design software. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Which word processing feature can be used to move an image next to a paragraph?
subQuestions.memoText: Text wrapping. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: An order form for the e-magazine is placed on the school's website. Which HTML tag AND attribute will be used to create a link to the order form?
subQuestions.memoText: <a> anchor tag; href attribute. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The e-magazine will be sold to learners and parents. Learners will use NFC payments to purchase the e-magazine. Explain how NFC payments are made.
subQuestions.memoText: Payments are made by bringing the POS and devices/bank card in close contact/tapping, allowing them to transfer data wirelessly. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Name TWO methods used to make online payments from home.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Online banking/EFT; electronic card payments; money sending service (e.g. Cash Send, eWallet); crypto currency; payment gateways e.g. PayPal (through your banking app). (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Your school will host a triathlon competition which includes swimming, running and bike riding. Learners from the school will assist by creating posters, taking photos and also with the general administration of the competition. The organisers from the school need to register participants. Briefly explain what information is.
subQuestions.memoText: Information is processed data that has meaning. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Suggest TWO reasons why the organisers should use electronic forms to register participants.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Accuracy; participants can complete the form in a shorter time/more efficient to complete by participants; less chance of processing errors; perform data validation; store/process/analyse information; share with/reach a larger audience; more environmentally friendly. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Posters about the event will be put up at various shopping centres to advertise the competition. Name ONE other method of advertising this event.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Flyers/stickers; online platforms e.g. social media; printed newspaper/magazines; billboards; radio/TV. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The posters contain a QR code. What happens when the QR code is scanned?
subQuestions.memoText: The QR code will provide a link to the website/document/additional information. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: The competition will raise money for a local charity as part of the school's social responsibility. Name an online method used to raise small amounts of money from a large number of people.
subQuestions.memoText: Crowdfunding. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give ONE example of a popular online platform to raise money.
subQuestions.memoText: Any ONE: Kickstarter; Indiegogo; GoFundMe; SeedInvest; Kiva; Patreon; CrowdQueb; Back a Buddy. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Specialised cameras will be used to capture the competition. Except for resolution, name TWO other camera specifications that impact the quality of the images.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Quality of the lens; quality/size/type of sensor; colour depth; contrast ratio; on-board software/software filters; ISO rating; digital vs optical zoom; image stabilisation; image processor; shutter speed; flash. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: Images will be transferred to a laptop via a card reader. State TWO advantages of a card reader.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Faster transfer of images to a computer from a digital camera; use less energy/power; photos can be transferred to the laptop without the camera being present; allows you to read from or write to many different cards. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The track layout below will be used for the competition. Participants will be issued with a device that is embedded with an RFID tag. The diagram, labelled 'Triathlon System Set-Up', shows a swim leg, then an entry gate with turnstiles and a nearby wireless (WiFi) router where participants enter a looping bike track marked BIKE, then an exit gate with turnstiles and another wireless router, followed by a run leg marked RUN leading to a finish line marked with a checkpoint scanner and a wireless-connected laptop station operated by an official. RFID/turnstile scanners are positioned at the entry, exit and finish points, each linked wirelessly back to the laptop station. What type of network is displayed?
subQuestions.memoText: WLAN/LAN/WAN. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Give TWO reasons why the school will be using RFID tags for the participants.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Tracking the participants' progress/safety during the race; keep record of participant's time; determining the position/rank of the participant. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: What technology does RFID tags use to transmit data?
subQuestions.memoText: Radio-frequency signals/radio waves. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: An autonomous car will capture the leading participants' progress. Define the concept autonomous car.
subQuestions.memoText: A self-driving car that can sense its environment and move safely with little or no human input. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: The school organisers will be on duty for many hours during the competition. They will be tracking all aspects of the event at their computer stations. Explain what ergonomic design is.
subQuestions.memoText: The design of furniture and other devices to make working more comfortable and safer. (1 mark)

subQuestions.questionText: Apart from ergonomically designed equipment, recommend TWO other ways for the organisers to prevent strain on their bodies.
subQuestions.memoText: Any TWO: Stand up and take regular breaks; sit up straight/back against the chair; stretch back/shoulders/neck; sit with both feet flat on the floor; don't slouch/bend your neck/correct posture; look away from the computer screen every 15 minutes. (2 marks)

subQuestions.questionText: After the competition, data was captured in a spreadsheet.
